Not backed: neither snapshot defines or lists 'wymagane' (required) permissions, or says how to tell a required system permission from an additional GDPR consent. The Android page treats every permission alike (accept or refuse). The item's own Ograniczenia#2 says no cited source settles this. The split in the title is the editors' synthesis.

claims.reason: Searched both cited snapshots for any text that says when a device or app permission counts as a GDPR consent, or the reverse. GDPR snapshot (full text, 88 pages): searched uprawnie*, aplikacj*, urządzeni*, 'system operacyjn*', 'ustawień technicznych' and read Art. 4 pkt 11, Art. 6 ust. 1 and Art. 7; no provision or recital links device permissions to consent. Nearest text is recital 32 (line 369: 'na wyborze ustawień technicznych do korzystania z usług społeczeństwa informacyjnego'), which lists choosing technical settings of information society services as one possible form of a consent act; it does not say when a system permission is a consent, so the absence claim holds. Android snapshot: searched RODO, zgod*, GDPR, 'dane osobowe', przetwarz*, prywatno*; the only hits are the menu names 'Prywatność' (lines 45, 105). Absence in the Android snapshot is absence from the stored main region of the page (4276 of 6655 characters).

claims.reason: Read the whole of Art. 7 (lines 2490-2513, full-text snapshot). Ust. 4 only says that, in judging voluntariness, account is taken 'w jak największym stopniu' of conditioning performance of a contract or service on consent not necessary for it. It states no rule on when a service must stay available after consent is refused. Note for the reviewer: recital 43 (lines 515-518) goes further than Art. 7 ust. 4: 'Zgody nie uważa się za dobrowolną, jeżeli ... od zgody uzależnione jest wykonanie umowy – w tym świadczenie usługi – mimo że do jej wykonania zgoda nie jest niezbędna.' The sentence is about Art. 7 ust. 4 only, so it holds.

claims.reason: The Android page says that enabling a permission affects how an app works and that after 'Nie zezwalaj' the app cannot use that permission. It does not state that particular app functions require particular access, nor that refusing a permission stops a function. The general statement is an inference from these lines, not a statement of the source. The GDPR snapshot speaks only of data processing necessary for a contract, not of app functions.

scope_gaps.note: The snapshot is the Polish text of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as printed in OJ L 119 of 4.5.2016. The sentence does not say that the duty binds only controllers within the territorial and material scope of the Regulation (Art. 2-3, not read in this check). A reader may assume every app provider is bound.

The page says that some of the steps work only on a Pixel phone with Android 15 or newer (line 13), and that it may contain AI-translated text (line 115). The sentence names no device; a reader may assume that all steps work on every Android phone.

The permission half rests on the Android help page only. The sentence says 'uprawnienie systemowe' without naming Android; a reader may assume the same holds for other operating systems, which no snapshot covers.
Generic statement about 'funkcje'; the only source is the Android permission page. No snapshot says which functions need which access.
